The model fixes an orientation and any additional spin or related lifting data required by its fields; these choices are its tangential structure. A **selected finite-regulator Euclidean model** on $K$ specifies its exact symmetry groups, field representations, finite field-value sets $X_\sigma$ for cells $\sigma\in K$, constraints, and configuration spaces $\Phi_x\subseteq\prod_{\sigma\in K}X_\sigma$ for each background $x$. It also specifies a dimensionless Euclidean action $S_x:\Phi_x\to\mathbb R$, finite measure weights $\mu_x:\Phi_x\to\mathbb C$, and a unital complex subalgebra $\mathcal O_x\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Phi_x,\mathbb C)$ of model-defined observables. For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$, write $\mathcal O_x(L)$ for the subalgebra of functions depending only on field variables on $L$; an observable is **local** if it belongs to $\mathcal O_x(L)$ for some specified $L$. A line observable has support on a one-dimensional subcomplex. Write $W_x(\phi):=\mu_x(\phi)e^{-S_x(\phi)}$. For local insertion functions $o_{j,x}:\Phi_x\to\mathbb C$, define the unnormalized correlator by $C_x(O_1,\ldots,O_n):=\sum_{\phi\in\Phi_x}W_x(\phi)\prod_{j=1}^n o_{j,x}(\phi)$; the empty tuple has value $Z_x=C_x()$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$; cochain labels, action phases, and the partition weight are dimensionless. The model separately assigns dimensions to any continuous field quantities or observables it includes. No continuum limit or Lorentzian continuation is part of this definition.

The ordinary-observable sum above is the no-defect sector of the model's **complete insertion functional**. For each background $x$, the model declares a set $\mathcal I_x$ of admissible inputs $I=(b;D;X_1,\ldots,X_n)$: $b$ specifies all remaining geometric and boundary data (there is no physical boundary for the closed $M$ here); $D$ is a finite decorated defect network; and each $X_j$ is a typed local, line, or other model-admitted insertion, possibly another decorated network. A network has finitely many smooth locally closed strata whose closures obey the frontier condition, the complete incidence relation, and model-specified field, orientation, coorientation, framing, and ordered junction data on each stratum, as in the topological-defect definition. The model states all disjointness, incidence, and label admissibility conditions. For every $I\in\mathcal I_x$ it supplies a finite set $\Omega_x(I)$ of field configurations, including any defect or junction variables and modified constraints, and a complex weight $w_x(I;\omega)$ with its declared normalization. Its unnormalized complete correlator is

$$
\widehat C_x(I):=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_x(I)}w_x(I;\omega)\in\mathbb C.
$$

For no defect and a tuple of ordinary local insertions this must reduce to $\Omega_x(I)=\Phi_x$ and $w_x(I;\phi)=W_x(\phi)\prod_j o_{j,x}(\phi)$, so $\widehat C_x(I)=C_x(O_1,\ldots,O_n)$. The empty network, empty insertion tuple has value $Z_x$. This is conditional finite model data, not a construction of defect correlators from the ordinary observable algebra or from the 2-group labels.

The regulator includes a precise support-move convention. Defect supports at the displayed regulator inputs are represented by subcomplexes, with their smooth strata and decorations specified. A permitted decorated isotopy preserves strata, incidence and ordered junctions, transports every label and framing, fixes $b$ and the background, and avoids all other insertions. A claim of topologicality along such a smooth path requires the model to supply complete correlators at every intermediate support and comparisons with the endpoint regulator inputs; if subdivisions or other regulator presentations are used, their field sums and comparison maps must be supplied. The model must verify equality of the complete correlators under these comparisons. At a fixed triangulation the same requirement applies to each declared discrete support move, with its exact transport of complete inputs. A path through supports not represented by subcomplexes is not evaluated merely by writing the fixed-$K$ ordinary sum. These extra assignments do not assert a continuum limit or triangulation independence.

Let $G$ be the selected finite discrete internal $0$-form symmetry group. Its action on the model's local field and observable data is specified by group homomorphisms into the corresponding automorphism groups. Let $A$ be the selected finite discrete abelian $1$-form symmetry group, written additively, with the exact support, charge, and background conventions of the selected p-form symmetry model. Choosing a finite Abelian $A$ is part of this 2-group model's input; no claim is made that every p-form symmetry group is Abelian without further hypotheses. The group is effective in the selected model: elements inducing identical actions in every admitted correlator, observable, and background are identified. Each generator $U_a(\Sigma)$ is a defect insertion with support $j(\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma$ is a smooth manifold without boundary and $j:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ is a smooth embedding with closed codimension-two image represented by a subcomplex of $K$; the insertion includes the model-specified local field or operator data and any required orientation, coorientation, framing, or junction data on that image. Following the selected p-form symmetry model, a **genuine line observable** is supported on a closed embedded one-dimensional submanifold, represented here by a one-dimensional subcomplex of $K$, and is defined without an attached higher-dimensional support; the model specifies its crossing junction and action. $$

$$

$$

$$

$$
a'_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1},\qquad \zeta^g_{ijk}=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk})+\beta(a'_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(a'_{ij},a'_{jk},g_k),
$$

$$
B'_{ijk}=\rho_{g_i}B_{ijk}+\zeta^g_{ijk}+\rho_{a'_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}.
$$

Horizontal composition sends $2$-arrow cochains $t,s$ to $s+\rho_h t$. For three consecutive arrows with vertex labels $g,h,k$, the associator is the vertex cochain $\sigma_i=\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$; identity arrows have vertex labels $e$ and edge labels $0$, and unit constraints are identity $2$-arrows. The pentagon and triangle coherence equations are those of this finite background gauge $2$-groupoid.

It must also transport weights by a configuration-independent nonzero scalar: there exists $c_F\in\mathbb C^\times$ with $W_y(T\phi)=c_FW_x(\phi)$ for every $\phi\in\Phi_x$. The scalar is not additional morphism data; it is unique when $W_x$ is not identically zero, while no uniqueness is asserted for zero-weight or empty fibers. The phase-law case requires a model-specified choice in $U(1)$, with the coherence stipulated below. Composition is $(S,\gamma)\circ(T,\alpha)=(S\circ T,\gamma\circ\alpha)$ and the identity is $(\operatorname{id}_{\Phi_x},\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_x})$. If $(J,j):F\Rightarrow F'$ and $(Q,q):H\Rightarrow H'$ with $F=(T,\alpha):D_x\to D_y$ and $H=(S,\gamma):D_y\to D_z$, their horizontal composite is $(Q\circ S\circ J\circ S^{-1},\ q\circ\gamma\circ j\circ\gamma^{-1}):H\circ F\Rightarrow H'\circ F'$. In the target $2$-category, locality preservation means $\alpha(\mathcal O_x(L))=\mathcal O_y(L)$ for each subcomplex $L\subseteq K$, and $j(\mathcal O_y(L))=\mathcal O_y(L)$ for each target-side $2$-morphism. Every $2$-morphism compares $1$-morphisms with the same source and target fibers. Vertical composites and inverses of $2$-morphisms preserve the target weight and local algebras.

Composing with $Q$ still preserves $W_z$. The algebra component is pullback by the inverse of the resulting configuration bijection and preserves each local subalgebra, because $q$, $\gamma$, $j$, and their inverses do so. Its source and target are correct since $(QSJS^{-1})(ST)=QSJT=S'T'$ and $(q\gamma j\gamma^{-1})(\gamma\alpha)=q\gamma j\alpha=\gamma'\alpha'$. Here $S'=QS$, $T'=JT$, $\gamma'=q\gamma$, and $\alpha'=j\alpha$.

Finally, for fixed parallel $1$-morphisms $(T,\alpha)$ and $(T',\alpha')$, any $2$-morphism is uniquely forced to have $J=T'T^{-1}$ and $j=\alpha'\alpha^{-1}$; it exists precisely when this pair meets the stated conditions. Consequently the hom categories have at most one arrow between any two objects. The displayed $1$-composition is strictly associative and unital. Every iterated horizontal composition, horizontal identity law, and either side of the interchange equation is now a well-typed $2$-morphism with the same source and target as its counterpart, so uniqueness proves the required equalities. This verifies that $\mathfrak M$ is a strict $2$-category.

Explicitly, it assigns a model fiber $D_x$ to each background object, a $1$-morphism $(T_f,\alpha_f)$ to each $1$-arrow, and a target-fiber $2$-morphism $(J_\eta,j_\eta)$ to each $2$-arrow $\eta:f\Rightarrow f'$. $$

$$

$$
F(a_{h,g,f})\circ\kappa_{h\circ g,f}\circ(\kappa_{h,g}\ast\operatorname{id}_{F(f)})=\kappa_{h,g\circ f}\circ(\operatorname{id}_{F(h)}\ast\kappa_{g,f}).
$$

$$
F(\ell_f)\circ\kappa_{\operatorname{id}_y,f}\circ(\iota_y\ast\operatorname{id}_{F(f)})=\operatorname{id}_{F(f)},\qquad F(r_f)\circ\kappa_{f,\operatorname{id}_x}\circ(\operatorname{id}_{F(f)}\ast\iota_x)=\operatorname{id}_{F(f)}.
$$

On the ordinary sector these reduce to the specified observable transport and $T_f$. For a $2$-arrow $\eta:f\Rightarrow f'$, the model supplies a bijection of target input data sending $f_*I$ to $f'_*I$ and a configuration bijection $\widetilde J_{\eta,I}:\Omega_y(f_*I)\to\Omega_y(f'_*I)$ with $\widetilde T_{f',I}=\widetilde J_{\eta,I}\widetilde T_{f,I}$ and preservation of the complete integrand. Comparison maps similarly run from $g_*(f_*I)$ to $(g\circ f)_*I$, with configuration maps from $\Omega_z(g_*f_*I)$ to $\Omega_z((g\circ f)_*I)$; unit maps run from $I$ to $(\operatorname{id}_x)_*I$. On each such fiber these maps obey the identity, vertical, horizontal, associator and unit equations displayed above, using their stated source and target inputs, and they intertwine every declared support move. Their weight transformation law is additional model data. In the coherent phase-law setting on complete inputs the model must in particular verify

$$
w_y(f_*I;\widetilde T_{f,I}\omega)=\chi_f(x)w_x(I;\omega)
$$

for every admitted $I$ and $\omega$, with the same configuration-independent phase and identity, composition and $2$-isomorphism conditions as below. This implies $\widehat C_y(f_*I)=\chi_f(x)\widehat C_x(I)$ by finite reindexing; ordinary-sector covariance alone does not establish this extension. Likewise, every claimed internal symmetry action on observables and defects includes a bijection on the complete typed insertion and combined background/boundary data, preserving admissibility and the complete correlator after that simultaneous transport; a specified anomalous background gauge transformation instead has its stated phase law. Crossing actions and their junctions must be defined on these complete inputs before a defect-charge relation is asserted.

Here $\ast$ denotes horizontal composition or whiskering of $2$-morphisms. These equations give the precise identity, vertical, horizontal, associator, and unit coherence required of the model assignment. The action and measure are model inputs; the finite 2-group data alone do not choose them or determine their transformation phase.

A permitted background counterterm is a model-declared dimensionless functional $L_x\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ that is a finite sum of functions, each depending only on cochain labels in one simplex or a specified finite cluster of simplices; it reweights the model by $e^{iL_x}$. The residual background anomaly is the class of these phases under $\chi_f(x)\mapsto e^{iL_y}\chi_f(x)e^{-iL_x}$ for the permitted counterterms. The anomaly is absent in the selected scheme exactly when an allowed counterterm makes every such phase $1$. The Postnikov class specifies the background constraint and gauge transformations; it is not itself the model's transformation phase or anomaly. It may enter an anomaly calculation for a specified action and measure.

A finite ordered simplicial complex $K$ has a finite vertex set with a total order and a collection of nonempty finite vertex subsets, called simplices, closed under taking nonempty subsets. Its dimension is the maximum of $|\sigma|-1$ over its simplices. A closed physical regulator is a finite ordered triangulation of a closed compact oriented smooth three-manifold; relative amplitudes are also defined on its finite ordered subcomplexes. The increasing vertex order orients every simplex.

Choose $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the trivial Abelian group $A=\{0\}$, the unique action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$, and the zero normalized Postnikov cocycle $\beta=0$. A background on $K$ is a flat edge cochain $a_{ij}\in G$, satisfying $a_{ij}+a_{jk}-a_{ik}=0$ on each ordered triangle; its face cochain $B$ is uniquely zero. A raw $1$-gauge arrow has vertex labels $g_i\in G$ and sends $a_{ij}$ to $a'_{ij}=g_i+a_{ij}-g_j$. The edge label $\lambda$ and vertex $2$-gauge label $t$ are necessarily zero, so this selected two-group is the ordinary finite $G$ symmetry regarded as a two-group with trivial $A$.

For each background $x=(a,0)$, the model's cell-value sets are $X_v=G$ at each vertex and a singleton at every positive-dimensional simplex. The configuration set is $\Phi_x=C^0(K;G)$, the set of spin assignments $\sigma=(\sigma_v)_{v\in K^{(0)}}$. There are no further constraints. Set the dimensionless action $S_x(\sigma)=0$, the finite measure weight $\mu_x(\sigma)=2^{-V_K}$, where $V_K$ is the number of vertices, and the observable algebra $\mathcal O_x=\operatorname{Fun}(\Phi_x,\mathbb C)$. A function is local when it depends on spins in a specified subcomplex. The local spin observable $m_v(\sigma)=(-1)^{\sigma_v}$ transforms nontrivially under the constant global $G$ action, so this $0$-form symmetry is effective. For a closed one-dimensional subcomplex $\gamma$, the product $\prod_{v\in\gamma^{(0)}}m_v(\sigma)$ is a line-supported observable defined without an attached surface. The selected $1$-form group is trivial: its only defect is $U_0(\Sigma)=1$, and the line observable has only the trivial $A$-character.

The complete defect-bearing input domain consists of any finite list of admitted ordinary spin functions, with their subcomplex supports, and any finite decorated network of the identity defect $U_0$. Every stratum has the trivial $A$ label, every junction has scalar $1$, and the model admits all choices of orientation or framing only with this same trivial response; the incidence and ordering data are recorded even though their factors are $1$. For each such input $I$, set $\Omega_x(I)=\Phi_x$ and

$$
w_x(I;\sigma)=2^{-V_K}\prod_j o_{j,x}(\sigma),\qquad \widehat C_x(I)=\sum_{\sigma\in C^0(K;G)}2^{-V_K}\prod_j o_{j,x}(\sigma).
$$

Thus every identity-network factor is exactly $1$ for every spin configuration. The combined boundary datum in the relative convention is the fixed background restriction $s$; no boundary spin value is fixed, and there is no additional boundary datum for a closed regulator. Gauge transport sends each spin by $T_g$ and every insertion function by pullback, transports the boundary background when it is allowed to vary, and preserves identity-network labels and junctions. Boundary-fixed relative gauge arrows restrict to $g=0$ on the boundary subcomplex. These are bijections of the complete inputs and configurations and preserve the displayed integrands with phase $1$; all comparison maps and $2$-arrow maps are identities under the strict translation composition law.

An identity support may be moved through any smooth decorated isotopy preserving incidence and avoiding the other supports: the model evaluates every intermediate identity network by exactly the same spin sum, including when its support is not a subcomplex of the fixed regulator. The endpoint comparison is the identity on spins and on ordinary insertion functions. If a supplied compatible subdivision $K'$ is used to represent a support, retain the old ordinary observables by pullback along restriction of vertex spins to $K$. Summing over the $V_{K'}-V_K$ new spins gives $2^{V_{K'}-V_K}2^{-V_{K'}}=2^{-V_K}$ for each old spin assignment, hence exactly the same complete correlator, for any supplied compatible refined background. This is a comparison for this identity response and these transported observables, not an assertion of triangulation independence of the separate background-gauging amplitude.

For a background gauge arrow with vertex labels $g$, the configuration bijection is $T_g(\sigma)_v=\sigma_v+g_v$ and the observable-algebra isomorphism is $\alpha_g(O)=O\circ T_g^{-1}$. These assignments respect identity and composition. The per-background partition weight is

$$
W_K(x)=Z_x=\sum_{\sigma\in\Phi_x}2^{-V_K}=1.
$$

The boundary state space on a subcomplex $L$ is the finite-dimensional space $\mathcal H(L)=\operatorname{Fun}(\pi_0\mathcal B(L),\mathbb C)$. For a fixed background $s$ on $L$, the relative convention fixes only this background restriction and sums over all spins on $K$ with weight $2^{-V_K}$; it does not fix boundary spin values. Thus the spin sector contributes $1$ for each extending background and introduces no additional seam factor. The relative background amplitude then uses the relative higher-gauge sum. All fields, action phases, measures, and amplitudes are dimensionless in the convention $\hbar=1$.

The closed-manifold data instantiate the finite-regulator two-group model interface. The relative subcomplex amplitudes and the background-only boundary state space are the additional boundary convention adopted here; they are not inferred from the closed-manifold interface. No continuum limit or empirical conclusion is part of this definition.

Let $K$ be a finite ordered oriented simplicial complex of dimension at most three in the relative extension of the selected model, with $V_K$ vertices and $E_K$ edges. For a closed physical regulator, $K$ is a finite ordered triangulation of a closed compact oriented smooth three-manifold. Use $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the trivial group $A=\{0\}$, the unique action $\rho$, the zero normalized Postnikov cocycle $\beta$, and the unit background response $W_K(x)=1$. The dynamical spin configurations for each background are $\Phi_x=C^0(K;G)$, with action $S_x=0$ and normalized measure $\mu_x(\sigma)=2^{-V_K}$. A background gauge arrow with vertex labels $g$ transports spins by $T_g(\sigma)=\sigma+g$ and transports observables by pullback.

For every background $x$, its spin partition weight is $Z_x=1$. The normalized background-gauging amplitude is
$$ Z_K^{(2)}=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(K)}\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}=\frac{1}{2^{V_K}}|\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)|. $$
For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ and fixed background $s$ on $L$, the relative background amplitude is
$$
Z_{K,L}^{(2)}(s)=2^{-(V_K-V_L)}|\{x\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K):x|_L=s\}|.
$$
If $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$ is a union of ordered subcomplexes with compatible restrictions and opposite induced seam orientations, the relative boundary amplitudes are gauge-invariant and obey
$$ Z_K^{(2)}=\sum_{[s]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(\Sigma)} Z_{K_2,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)Z_{K_1,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}. $$
For a one-vertex boundary complex the amplitude is $1/2$. These conclusions concern only the specified finite model; they do not establish a continuum quantum field theory or empirical behavior.

Adopt as the finite physical model the three-dimensional vertex-spin regulator with $G=\mathbb Z/2$, trivial $1$-form group $A=\{0\}$, zero Postnikov cocycle, zero action, and the normalized uniform measure on spins. Its global $G$ symmetry flips every spin, its background response is the unit weight for every flat background, and its selected boundary state space and relative amplitudes are those specified by the model definition. The finite background gauging and sewing prescription is part of this adopted model. This postulate says nothing about a continuum limit, an empirical realization, or the truth of any more general quantum field theory.
